about: Generated by scripts/ark-canopy-moves.mts from the signature behaviours catalogue (each quote an exact span of the species' stored text). species: {slug: [mode (brachiate | leap | run), 1 when a prehensile tail grips branches, the deciding quote]}. Only kinds whose behaviour profile climbs.

binturong: Prehensile tail that works like a fifth limb in the canopy
black-giant-squirrel: It crosses gaps between trees in long, agile leaps.
bornean-orangutan: Long arms and strong hands for canopy movement
lar-gibbon: Travelling through the canopy, it swings arm over arm and at speed lets go with both hands, flying briefly across gaps between trees before catching the next branch.
mantled-guereza: Colobus monkeys make long, striking leaps between branches in the forest canopy, using their long limbs and flowing tails for balance and propulsion.
mantled-howler-monkey: Mantled Howler Monkeys use a prehensile tail like a fifth limb in the canopy.
siamang: The Throat-Sac Canopy Duet Singer, carrying Union through swinging movement, bonded calls, and a voice that makes family presence travel through rainforest.
southern-tamandua: They climb well using a strong prehensile tail.
spotted-cuscus: The prehensile tail has a bare roughened underside and grips branches like an additional limb, keeping the animal anchored while it moves.
squirrel-monkey: It runs along branches on all fours and does not swing.
tayra: Strong claws and a long balancing tail let it run along branches and leap from one tree to the next.
tufted-capuchin: Thick, furred tail curled around branches as a grip
white-faced-saki: White-faced Sakis move through the forest canopy primarily by powerful bounds and leaps between branches, covering significant distances in the air.
